notes:
Account summary
- Regulated EU customer (banking-adjacent / reg reporting). Wants Redwood Private in AWS VPC first, but is explicitly planning for on-prem later ("we will need to bring this behind our DC firewall next year").
- Primary concern is networking + auditability more than model quality. They have an internal security review committee and a separate network engineering org (slow approvals).

Current deployment posture / constraints (from calls + emails)
- AWS accounts are centrally governed. VPC is managed by a shared platform team.
- Hard constraint: no internet egress from workload subnets (no IGW, no NAT) for prod. Exceptions require VP sign-off.
- Prefer private connectivity: interface endpoints + gateway endpoints only. They asked if Redwood installer ever requires direct calls to public AWS APIs.
- DNS: they run centralized Route53 Resolver rules (forwarding to corporate DNS). They want to understand any private DNS toggles required for endpoints.
- Logging: they want VPC Flow Logs enabled and routed to their central logging account. Retention target mentioned: 365 days online, 7 years archive (final sink TBD).
- Encryption/KMS: customer-managed KMS keys required for logs and any bucket storage. Wants confirmation we don’t require sharing keys with Redwood.

Workload / scale (rough)
- Use cases: internal compliance Q&A over policies + case notes (doc-search), summarization of long regulatory filings, and an internal support-agent workflow.
- Early targets: ~50–150 concurrent users; peak bursts during reporting cycles.
- Latency: "interactive" for chat; no strict number given but they flagged >3s as problematic.
- Data handling: PII present; they want strict audit logging for admin actions + network traffic visibility.

Product interest / architecture direction
- Phase 1: Redwood Private (VPC) with locked-down networking. They explicitly want an opinionated VPC baseline (subnet tiering, endpoints, SG defaults) to reduce internal variance.
- Phase 2: on-prem package (not in scope for alpha), but they want assurance the VPC approach won’t paint them into a corner.
